players.name: DPFSGJ99
players.tagline: A glorious disaster with a putter and a shovel for a short game.
players.body: DPFSGJ99 got buried in the net race, finishing 49th net and 50th gross while carding +23 net and +30 gross. The damage was everywhere: -27.5 total strokes gained, with the short game taking the biggest beating at -15.84 and putting another -5.77, which is how you turn a round into a landfill. The card backs it up with 34 putts, five 3-putts, zero fairways hit, and only 5 greens in regulation, so yeah, there was not much salvaging this thing. The blow-up sequence was ugly even by simulator standards: hole 13 went for 7, hole 15 went for 7, and hole 16 was the monster crater at 10 on a par 3, a full seven over with no shot detail to romanticize it. The one tiny bright spot was a couple of par-3 pokes that landed inside the margin, but they were just speed bumps in a round that never found a pulse.

players.name: VlakatafakatA
players.tagline: A lot of putts holed just to keep this from becoming a full train wreck.
players.body: VlakatafakatA was right behind in the net pileup, 50th net and 47th gross, with +25 net and +15 gross. The raw golf was still rough but a touch less radioactive than the card result suggests: -13.5 total strokes gained, led by -10.31 tee to green and -7.48 around the greens, while the putting was also a drag at -3.2. The stats say this one was a weird mix of damage and survival: 6 greens in regulation, 33 putts, five 3-putts, and 110 feet of putts made, which is basically the golf equivalent of bailing water with a teaspoon while the hull’s already cracked. He did have a couple of clean par-3 looks early with deuces on holes 2 and 4, but the wheels came off on the par-3s at 6, 10, and 14, each making 6 or worse in net terms and leaving the round with too much smoke and not enough fire. No prior event history to build a trend from, just one very ugly baseline of what happens when the ball-striking and the save shots both decide to ghost.
